text: @dr-co/dsh-skills 是面向 DSH Web GUI 的技能管理插件，通过侧边栏 Skills 面板汇总 DSH home 下的技能、安装插件包内附带的技能，以及插件通过 skills 服务提供的技能。用户可查看技能内容，并对自己的技能进行编辑、重命名、启用或停用；也可下载 SKILL.md 或整个目录，并上传新技能或替换现有技能。面板区分可写的用户技能与只读的插件技能，提供英语和俄语界面。适合需要在 Web GUI 集中整理 DSH 技能的用户；不需要 API key，默认使用 DSH home 下的 skills 目录。

@dr-co/dsh-skills adds a DSH Web GUI Skills panel. It lists user, plugin-bundled, and host-provided skills. Users can view and manage their own skills, download them, or upload and replace them. Plugin-bundled skills are read-only. The interface supports English and Russian.
想在 DSH 网页界面里查看和整理已经安装的技能。
怎么区分自己目录里的技能和插件自带的技能？
我想在浏览器里直接编辑某个技能的 SKILL.md。
有没有办法把一个技能目录打包下载，之后再上传回来？
I want to enable or disable a DSH skill from the web interface.
Can I upload a new skill or replace one from the Skills panel?
@dr-co/dsh-skills 功能「技能目录汇总」：面板合并显示 DSH home 中的用户技能、安装插件包内的技能，以及 skills 服务提供但没有文件的技能，并呈现来源和状态。
@dr-co/dsh-skills 功能「技能查看与编辑」：选择技能可查看其文本；用户技能可编辑并保存，插件包内的技能和无文件的提供型技能按只读内容展示。
@dr-co/dsh-skills feature “Skill transfer”: Download a skill file or folder; upload a ZIP to create or replace one.
@dr-co/dsh-skills 的维护与更新元数据：已归档；距最后推送 19 天；提交数 7；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 22/100（置信度 low）。

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · @dr-co/dsh-skills：A **Skills page** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI: a sidebar row that opens a full main panel listing every skill the host knows about — our own, the ones bundled inside installed packages, and the ones a plugin provides without any file — with download, upload, rename, enable/disable, and editing built in.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · @dr-co/dsh-skills：The page reads the filesystem itself instead of asking `ctx.skills` alone, because that service only reports the skills it can load. A skill whose file is named `_SKILL.md` is invisible to the core on purpose — and it is exactly the one you need to see when a skill stops working.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · What it does：| Section | Where it comes from | Colours | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Standard skills in `$DSH_HOME/skills`** | our own directories | green dot when active, grey when disabled, normal name colour | everything: view, edit, rename, upload, both downloads, enable/disable |
| **Skills bundled with plugins** | `<pkg>/skills/*` and `<pkg>/assets/*` of every installed package, found through their manifests | pink dot and pink name when active, grey-pink when disabled | view and both downloads — they live in `node_modules` |
| **Provided by plugins (no file)** | `ctx.skills.list()` entries with no file on disk | pink, dashed dot | view and `Download SKILL.md`; no ZIP, because there is no directory to archive |

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · What it does：- **Status** is one 11px dot: green for `SKILL.md`, grey for `_SKILL.md` (ours); pink for an active packaged skill, grey-pink for a disabled one. A directory holding both files is reported as a conflict, in red. The word lives in the dot's tooltip and accessible name, not in the row.
- **Name** takes every pixel the row has left, with the frontmatter `description` underneath; both are cut with an ellipsis, never wrapped.
- **Path** is relative to `$DSH_HOME` when it is inside it, otherwise relative to the package; shown in full up to 15 characters and, past that, as its first 7 and last 7 around three dots (`split/p...ath/foo`). The full path is in the tooltip. Below 640px the column is not rendered at all and the row keeps the path in its accessible name.
- **View** — the first item in every row's menu, for all three sections. It opens the same full-page frame as the editor but read-only: the raw text, no `textarea`, no `Save`, a `Read-only` badge, `Close` back to the list, and `Edit` beside it when the skill may be edited. Nothing is rendered — no markdown, no highlighting — and nothing can be written from it. A provider skill's text comes

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Colours and themes：Green and grey are the shell's own tokens (`--dsw-alias-state-success-primary` for on, `--dsw-alias-state-idle-primary` for off), so they match the rest of the interface in every theme for free. Pink is not in the token set, so the plugin defines two variables of its own and gives both palettes their own values:

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Colours and themes：| Palette | `--dshsk-plugin-accent` | contrast on the panel | `--dshsk-plugin-accent-muted` | contrast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| light (`#ffffff`) | `#c2185b` | 5.87:1 | `#8d5f72` | 5.23:1 |
| dark (`#232324`) | `#f472b6` | 5.93:1 | `#c98ba6` | 5.78:1 |

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Colours and themes：Both clear the 4.5:1 bar for text and the 3:1 bar for the dot, and both are above the shell's green on white (2.28:1). The dark block keys off `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` — the attribute the shell's own theme presenter writes when it applies a snapshot — and *not* off `prefers-color-scheme`, because the resolved scheme follows the user's setting (including "system" dark and registered themes), not the operating system. The test recomputes both ratios from the values in `src/client/styles.js`.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：The page button and the row menu are not the same operation, and the difference is deliberate: a stray drop should not be able to overwrite a working skill.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：| Upload | Accepted | Name comes from | If the name is taken |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Page button (create)** | only a ZIP with one top-level folder containing `SKILL.md` | the folder name (kebab-case) | refused: *a skill with this name already exists* — replace it from the row menu instead |
| **Row menu (replace)** | a single `SKILL.md`, or a ZIP whose folder is this skill's own name | the row | — (this is the only way to replace) |

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：A new skill is created from a zip whose top-level folder is the skill name; a single `SKILL.md` is only accepted when replacing an existing skill. Everything else — several top-level entries, `SKILL.md` at the archive root, an archive without `SKILL.md`, an illegal folder name, a broken archive, a non-ZIP file for the create upload, a file not named `SKILL.md` for the replace upload — is refused with `Unrecognized skill format` («Нераспознаваемый формат скилла») and nothing on disk changes.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：Safety, in the order it happens: every path is resolved and proved to stay inside its root (traversal segments, absolute paths, drive letters and leading dots are refused before the filesystem sees them); a skill directory and its file must be real — a symlinked `SKILL.md` is skipped by the list and never read, written, or archived; a packaged skill is refused by the *host* for every write (`403 read-only`), not merely hidden by the browser; uploads are capped; a ZIP is unpacked into a dot-prefixed staging directory and swapped in by rename only after every member has validated, with the previous directory restored if the swap fails; file modes from the archive are preserved. A refused upload leaves the tree byte-identical, which is what the tests assert.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Install：The package ships a `dsh.bundle` layer, so `dsh plugin add` both installs it and mounts it; it then appears in the settings plugin list where it can be switched off or removed.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dr-co/dsh-skills
```

From a checkout, while developing:

```sh
npm install
npm run build
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:$PWD
```

Restart the Web GUI afterwards. The sidebar gains a **Skills** row after Plugins and Tasks.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Configuration：```yaml
- id: dsh-skills
  name: '@dr-co/dsh-skills'
  config:
    dshHome: /home/dsh/work/ai/.dsh   # default: $DSH_HOME, then ~/.dsh

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Configuration：The home follows the harness' own precedence — an explicit `dshHome`, then `$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh` — with a leading `~` expanded. A blank `$DSH_HOME` counts as unset, so a blank variable never resolves the path to the working directory. The installation is found by walking up from the running `dsh` entry point to the package whose manifest is named `@deepseek-ai/dsh`; across its `node_modules` and every profile's `node_modules`, packages are read from their manifests only (a package's own `node_modules` is never descended into). Packaged skills are cached for 30 seconds — they cannot change under a running host except by an install — and our own skills are always read live.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Host API：| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/skills` | home, roots, and every row with its `actions` |
| `GET` | `/skill/<id>` | the text: a file's contents, or a provider skill's body from `ctx.skills.get()` |
| `PUT` | `/skill/<id>` | `{content}` → writes atomically, preserves mode and status |
| `POST` | `/skill/<id>/enable` · `/disable` | rename the file, the harness' own switch |
| `POST` | `/skill/<id>/rename` | `{name}` → rename the directory inside its parent |
| `GET` | `/skill/<id>/download.md` | exact file bytes |
| `GET` | `/skill/<id>/download.zip` | whole directory, rooted at its name |
| `POST` | `/upload?mode=create` | a ZIP that creates a new skill |
| `POST` | `/upload?mode=replace&id=<id>` | a file or ZIP that replaces that row's skill |

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Host API：A row id is `<origin>:<rootKey>:<relative path>` (`user:home:skills/foo`), resolved against the live catalog on every call — an id the catalog does not have is `not-found`, never a path to read.

Codes: `unrecognized-format` (415), `name-mismatch` (409), `already-exists` (409), `conflict` (409), `read-only` (403), `not-found` (404), `too-large` (413), `bad-request` (400), `write-failed` (500). The English `error` field is a diagnostic; the page shows its own language by code.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Host API：**Access control is the deployment's, not the plugin's.** These are plain same-origin routes on the Web GUI's own listener: anyone who can reach the GUI can list, read, download, save, and upload skills. That matches what the GUI already grants (a session with shell access), and the harness binds itself to a single interface, but a deployment that exposes the GUI publicly should put its own authentication in front of the whole origin — the plugin adds none.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Platform notes (what a plugin cannot do)：- **The sidebar cannot be extended by adding a slot.** The `sidebar` slot is `kind: 'single'` and occupied by the shell's own `SidebarRoot`. The supported extension point is the list slot it declares, `sidebar.panellist` (`SidebarPanelIconOwnerProps { size, active }`), where the entry's `id` must equal the `main` slot's key (`MainPanelId`). This plugin registers exactly that, plus `ctx.slots.register({ name: 'main', key: 'dsh-skills', locale: NS }, SkillsPage)` — a real main panel, not a dialog. Panel switching is the shell's `ctx.layout.selectPanel(id)`. The icon is drawn inline at 24×24, `stroke="currentColor"`, `stroke-width="1.75"`, `fill="none"`, round joins, and honouring the `size` the shell passes.
- **No shared markdown renderer is importable.** The client module table is fixed (`react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `react-dom`, `react-dom/client`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `zod`, `@tanstack/react-virtual`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-dockkit`); Shiki and the harness' markdown component live *inside* the shel

A directory holding both files is reported as a conflict, in red. The word lives in the dot's tooltip and accessible name, not in the row.
- **Name** takes every pixel the row has left, with the frontmatter `description` underneath; both are cut with an ellipsis, never wrapped.
- **Path** is relative to `$DSH_HOME` when it is inside it, otherwise relative to the package; shown in full up to 15 characters and, past that, as its first 7 and last 7 around three dots (`split/p...ath/foo`). The full path is in the tooltip. Below 640px the column is not rendered at all and the row keeps the path in its accessible name.
- **View** — the first item in every row's menu, for all three sections. It opens the same full-page frame as the editor but read-only: the raw text, no `textarea`, no `Save`, a `Read-only` badge, `Close` back to the list, and `Edit` beside it when the skill may be edited. Nothing is rendered — no markdown, no highlighting — and nothing can be written from it. A provider skill's text comes

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Colours and themes：Green and grey are the shell's own tokens (`--dsw-alias-state-success-primary` for on, `--dsw-alias-state-idle-primary` for off), so they match the rest of the interface in every theme for free. Pink is not in the token set, so the plugin defines two variables of its own and gives both palettes their own values:

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Colours and themes：| Palette | `--dshsk-plugin-accent` | contrast on the panel | `--dshsk-plugin-accent-muted` | contrast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| light (`#ffffff`) | `#c2185b` | 5.87:1 | `#8d5f72` | 5.23:1 |
| dark (`#232324`) | `#f472b6` | 5.93:1 | `#c98ba6` | 5.78:1 |

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Colours and themes：Both clear the 4.5:1 bar for text and the 3:1 bar for the dot, and both are above the shell's green on white (2.28:1). The dark block keys off `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` — the attribute the shell's own theme presenter writes when it applies a snapshot — and *not* off `prefers-color-scheme`, because the resolved scheme follows the user's setting (including "system" dark and registered themes), not the operating system. The test recomputes both ratios from the values in `src/client/styles.js`.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：The page button and the row menu are not the same operation, and the difference is deliberate: a stray drop should not be able to overwrite a working skill.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：| Upload | Accepted | Name comes from | If the name is taken |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Page button (create)** | only a ZIP with one top-level folder containing `SKILL.md` | the folder name (kebab-case) | refused: *a skill with this name already exists* — replace it from the row menu instead |
| **Row menu (replace)** | a single `SKILL.md`, or a ZIP whose folder is this skill's own name | the row | — (this is the only way to replace) |

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：A new skill is created from a zip whose top-level folder is the skill name; a single `SKILL.md` is only accepted when replacing an existing skill. Everything else — several top-level entries, `SKILL.md` at the archive root, an archive without `SKILL.md`, an illegal folder name, a broken archive, a non-ZIP file for the create upload, a file not named `SKILL.md` for the replace upload — is refused with `Unrecognized skill format` («Нераспознаваемый формат скилла») and nothing on disk changes.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：Safety, in the order it happens: every path is resolved and proved to stay inside its root (traversal segments, absolute paths, drive letters and leading dots are refused before the filesystem sees them); a skill directory and its file must be real — a symlinked `SKILL.md` is skipped by the list and never read, written, or archived; a packaged skill is refused by the *host* for every write (`403 read-only`), not merely hidden by the browser; uploads are capped; a ZIP is unpacked into a dot-prefixed staging directory and swapped in by rename only after every member has validated, with the previous directory restored if the swap fails; file modes from the archive are preserved.
```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dr-co/dsh-skills
```

From a checkout, while developing:

```sh
npm install
npm run build
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:$PWD
```

Restart the Web GUI afterwards. The sidebar gains a **Skills** row after Plugins and Tasks.

- id: dsh-skills
  name: '@dr-co/dsh-skills'
  config:
    dshHome: /home/dsh/work/ai/.dsh   # default: $DSH_HOME, then ~/.dsh

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Configuration：The home follows the harness' own precedence — an explicit `dshHome`, then `$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh` — with a leading `~` expanded. @dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：A new skill is created from a zip whose top-level folder is the skill name; a single `SKILL.md` is only accepted when replacing an existing skill. Everything else — several top-level entries, `SKILL.md` at the archive root, an archive without `SKILL.md`, an illegal folder name, a broken archive, a non-ZIP file for the create upload, a file not named `SKILL.md` for the replace upload — is refused with `Unrecognized skill format` («Нераспознаваемый формат скилла») and nothing on disk changes.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Two uploads, two contracts：Safety, in the order it happens: every path is resolved and proved to stay inside its root (traversal segments, absolute paths, drive letters and leading dots are refused before the filesystem sees them); a skill directory and its file must be real — a symlinked `SKILL.md` is skipped by the list and never read, written, or archived; a packaged skill is refused by the *host* for every write (`403 read-only`), not merely hidden by the browser; uploads are capped; a ZIP is unpacked into a dot-prefixed staging directory and swapped in by rename only after every member has validated, with the previous directory restored if the swap fails; file modes from the archive are preserved. A refused upload leaves the tree byte-identical, which is what the tests assert.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Install：The package ships a `dsh.bundle` layer, so `dsh plugin add` both installs it and mounts it; it then appears in the settings plugin list where it can be switched off or removed.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @dr-co/dsh-skills
```

From a checkout, while developing:

```sh
npm install
npm run build
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:$PWD
```

Restart the Web GUI afterwards. The sidebar gains a **Skills** row after Plugins and Tasks.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Configuration：```yaml
- id: dsh-skills
  name: '@dr-co/dsh-skills'
  config:
    dshHome: /home/dsh/work/ai/.dsh   # default: $DSH_HOME, then ~/.dsh

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Configuration：The home follows the harness' own precedence — an explicit `dshHome`, then `$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh` — with a leading `~` expanded. A blank `$DSH_HOME` counts as unset, so a blank variable never resolves the path to the working directory. The installation is found by walking up from the running `dsh` entry point to the package whose manifest is named `@deepseek-ai/dsh`; across its `node_modules` and every profile's `node_modules`, packages are read from their manifests only (a package's own `node_modules` is never descended into). Packaged skills are cached for 30 seconds — they cannot change under a running host except by an install — and our own skills are always read live.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Host API：| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/skills` | home, roots, and every row with its `actions` |
| `GET` | `/skill/<id>` | the text: a file's contents, or a provider skill's body from `ctx.skills.get()` |
| `PUT` | `/skill/<id>` | `{content}` → writes atomically, preserves mode and status |
| `POST` | `/skill/<id>/enable` · `/disable` | rename the file, the harness' own switch |
| `POST` | `/skill/<id>/rename` | `{name}` → rename the directory inside its parent |
| `GET` | `/skill/<id>/download.md` | exact file bytes |
| `GET` | `/skill/<id>/download.zip` | whole directory, rooted at its name |
| `POST` | `/upload?mode=create` | a ZIP that creates a new skill |
| `POST` | `/upload?mode=replace&id=<id>` | a file or ZIP that replaces that row's skill |

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Host API：A row id is `<origin>:<rootKey>:<relative path>` (`user:home:skills/foo`), resolved against the live catalog on every call — an id the catalog does not have is `not-found`, never a path to read.

Codes: `unrecognized-format` (415), `name-mismatch` (409), `already-exists` (409), `conflict` (409), `read-only` (403), `not-found` (404), `too-large` (413), `bad-request` (400), `write-failed` (500). The English `error` field is a diagnostic; the page shows its own language by code.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Host API：**Access control is the deployment's, not the plugin's.** These are plain same-origin routes on the Web GUI's own listener: anyone who can reach the GUI can list, read, download, save, and upload skills. That matches what the GUI already grants (a session with shell access), and the harness binds itself to a single interface, but a deployment that exposes the GUI publicly should put its own authentication in front of the whole origin — the plugin adds none.

@dr-co/dsh-skills README · Platform notes (what a plugin cannot do)：- **The sidebar cannot be extended by adding a slot.** The `sidebar` slot is `kind: 'single'` and occupied by the shell's own `SidebarRoot`. The supported extension point is the list slot it declares, `sidebar.panellist` (`SidebarPanelIconOwnerProps { size, active }`), where the entry's `id` must equal the `main` slot's key (`MainPanelId`). This plugin registers exactly that, plus `ctx.slots.register({ name: 'main', key: 'dsh-skills', locale: NS }, SkillsPage)` — a real main panel, not a dialog. Panel switching is the shell's `ctx.layout.selectPanel(id)`. The icon is drawn inline at 24×24, `stroke="currentColor"`, `stroke-width="1.75"`, `fill="none"`, round joins, and honouring the `size` the shell passes.
- **No shared markdown renderer is importable.** The client module table is fixed (`react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `react-dom`, `react-dom/client`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `zod`, `@tanstack/react-virtual`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-dockkit`); Shiki and the harness' markdown component live *inside* the shel
